title: The Rising Cost of Electric Power—and What to Do About It
gist: BCG argues rising electricity costs are structural, not a fading 2022 fuel shock, driven by supply-demand imbalances, a T&D capex supercycle, and regulations built for flat demand; residential bills outpaced inflation in 80% of OECD countries since 2010 and US prices have risen >7%/yr since 2021. PJM, where capacity prices jumped from $29 to >$300/MW-day and data centers drove 46% of charges, is the leading indicator, and BCG prescribes near-term cost reallocation, medium-term utility efficiency, and long-term market redesign.

insights.claim: Global electricity demand is now growing faster than demand for any other major energy source, with the sharpest shift in developed markets where consumption had been flat for about 15 years.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Ends the flat-load era for developed-market utilities; supports long-duration capex and generation demand themes.
insights.quote: Global demand for electricity is now growing faster than for any other major energy source.

insights.claim: In summer 2026 the US lower 48 states set a run of weekly electric output records per the Edison Electric Institute, and three of the largest grid operators set monthly peak-demand records, one breaking a 20-year-old record.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Peak demand tightness supports capacity prices and peaker/storage economics.

insights.claim: Residential electricity bills have grown faster than inflation in 80% of OECD countries since 2010, across liberalized and vertically integrated markets, coal-heavy and renewables-rich grids alike.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Affordability pressure is systemic, not market-specific, so political/regulatory risk to utilities is broad-based.
insights.quote: Residential electricity bills have grown faster than inflation in 80% of OECD countries since 2010.
insights.locator: Demand increases are only the latest

insights.claim: BCG argues the view that power prices will revert to historical norms as post-2022 Ukraine-war fuel shocks fade is likely too optimistic, because prices that came off 2022-2024 peaks settled well above prior levels and the cost drivers do not track fuel cycles.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite mean reversion in power prices; structural drivers imply persistently elevated tariffs.
insights.quote: We believe that’s potentially too optimistic.
insights.locator: One interpretation is that these increases

insights.claim: High energy costs are driving industrial relocation: 9% of UK manufacturers are shifting production abroad (Make UK), a third of German industrial manufacturers are moving capacity out (German Chamber of Commerce), and 20% of German companies across industries are moving or considering it.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Deindustrialization risk for UK/Germany; favors low-cost-power jurisdictions for energy-intensive investment.
insights.quote: A third of industrial manufacturers are moving capacity out of the country, according to an analysis by the German Chamber of Commerce

insights.claim: New energy-intensive industrial projects are increasingly sited in lower-energy-cost locations, which slows growth in high-cost countries and can erode national economic competitiveness.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Power cost is becoming a primary site-selection variable, a tailwind for cheap-power regions.

themes.theme: Three cost drivers: supply gap, grid capex, legacy rules

insights.claim: The core task for generators has flipped from replacing retiring fossil assets with renewables to serve flat loads to adding net new capacity, requiring renewables, gas and in some markets nuclear simply to keep pace with demand.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Supports all-of-the-above generation build-out; gas and nuclear benefit alongside renewables.

insights.claim: Interconnection queue backlogs delay access to the cheapest new power sources and force continued reliance on higher-cost incumbent resources, while thinning reserve margins raise the cost of serving peak demand.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Incumbent generators capture scarcity rents while queues persist; queue reform is a key price catalyst.
insights.quote: backlogs in interconnection queues delay access to some of the cheapest new power sources

insights.claim: Where demand falls, as in the UK, fixed grid costs are spread over a smaller user base, raising the burden on each customer.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Falling volumes can raise unit tariffs, a self-reinforcing affordability problem in Europe.
insights.locator: In other markets where demand is falling

insights.claim: Transmission and distribution spending is climbing steeply after decades of underinvestment, driven by aging infrastructure, data center connections, offshore wind interconnection, extreme-weather resilience and electrification, at a scale unseen in decades.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Multi-year T&D capex supercycle benefits grid equipment suppliers and rate-base growth but pressures bills.
insights.quote: The scale of investment now underway in many markets is unlike anything the industry has seen in decades.

insights.claim: Volumetric cost-recovery rules designed for flat demand and falling costs cannot distinguish peak from off-peak consumption, so as peaks rise and metered volume falls (notably in Europe), utilities spread fixed costs over a shrinking base and cannot recover the cost of batteries, smart charging or demand response.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Rate design reform is a precondition for flexibility/storage investment returns.
insights.locator: Regulations Designed for Different Market Conditions

insights.claim: Net metering, effective in launching rooftop solar, now shifts grid costs onto non-solar customers as solar nears mass adoption; Belgium and the Netherlands have moved away from it but it remains prevalent elsewhere.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Expect further net-metering rollbacks, a headwind for residential solar economics.
insights.quote: it essentially shifts overall grid costs onto customers who don’t have solar

themes.theme: US as leading indicator and utility risk loop

insights.claim: US average electricity prices were flat in nominal terms through the 2010s, but since 2021 nominal prices have risen more than 7% annually through mid-2026, with the US having the fastest load growth in the developed world.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Sustained >7% tariff growth heightens political risk for US regulated utilities.
insights.quote: the pattern broke in 2021, with nominal prices rising more than 7% annually through mid-2026
insights.locator: A Leading Indicator: The US Market

insights.claim: Mentions of affordability on earnings calls of the 29 largest publicly traded US utilities rose fourfold from 2019 to 2026.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Affordability is now a core investor concern in utility equity valuation.

insights.claim: Pew Research found 64% of US consumers cite utilities wanting to make more money as a major reason for rising power costs, more than any other factor including data center growth.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Public blame targets utility profits, raising risk of ROE cuts and rate-case pushback.
insights.quote: Pew Research found that 64% of US consumers cite utility companies wanting to make more money as a major reason for rising costs.
insights.locator: The public is seeking someone to blame

insights.claim: US state and federal officials are intervening directly in rate cases and exploring compensation caps, bans on billing certain expenses, and income-based rate relief.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Regulatory lag and allowed-return risk rising for US utilities.

insights.claim: Moody's and Fitch Ratings cite elevated electricity costs as a potential credit risk for US utilities, meaning affordability is becoming a financial variable in credit ratings.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Watch utility credit spreads and ratings actions tied to affordability.
insights.quote: Some agencies, including Moody’s and Fitch Ratings, cite elevated electricity costs as a potential credit risk for US utilities.

insights.claim: BCG warns of a doom loop in which rising costs trigger scrutiny and regulatory risk, leading to credit concerns that raise utilities' cost of capital and push costs even higher.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Reflexive risk: higher cost of capital can compound tariff growth and pressure utility multiples.
insights.quote: rising costs trigger more scrutiny and regulatory risk, which leads to credit concerns, in turn raising the cost of capital for utilities and pushing costs even higher

insights.claim: A second doom loop is possible where rising power costs undermine the economics of electrifying heating and similar loads, so less electrification spreads fixed costs over fewer users and raises costs further.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Risk to heat-pump/electrification demand forecasts underpinning grid capex plans.

themes.theme: PJM capacity shock and data centers

insights.claim: PJM Interconnection, the largest US wholesale power market serving 67 million people in 13 states and DC, hosts the densest data center load in the country in northern Virginia.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: PJM is the epicenter where data center demand meets supply constraints.
insights.locator: Within the US, one market clearly

insights.claim: PJM capacity auction prices rose from $29 per MW-day for 2024-2025 delivery to more than $300 per MW-day for 2026-2029.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Roughly 10x capacity repricing is a windfall for PJM generators with available capacity.
insights.quote: rising from $29 per MWD for 2024–2025 delivery to more than $300 per MWD for 2026–2029

insights.claim: PJM's independent market monitor attributes 46% of capacity market charges over the last four auctions to data center loads.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Data centers are a measurable driver of consumer bills, inviting large-load tariff policy.
insights.quote: market charges attributable to data center loads represented 46% of the total

insights.claim: Because capacity costs reach retail bills with a lag, a substantial share of PJM's already-cleared increases has yet to appear on customer statements, making further retail price increases likely.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Expect further retail bill increases and political backlash in PJM states.
insights.quote: a substantial share of the increase already cleared has yet to show up on customer statements
insights.locator: Two features make PJM a leading indicator

insights.claim: Political response in PJM has arrived faster than the bills, with officials challenging market and governance structure, turning once-technical market design into public debate.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Market rule changes (caps, redesign) are a key risk to merchant generator upside.
insights.locator: Two features make PJM a leading indicator

insights.claim: MISO's rates have risen less than inflation thanks to a large renewables build-out and production tax credits, but rising demand and utility capex growing 11% a year through 2030 (versus 6% in PJM) will likely push its prices higher over time.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: MISO may be the next affordability hotspot; MISO utilities have strong rate-base growth.
insights.quote: utility capex is set to grow at 11% a year through 2030 (compared to just 6% in PJM)
insights.locator: PJM is starting to take action

insights.claim: How data-center-driven load growth is resolved market by market may be the largest single swing factor for affordability in the US and most markets worldwide over the next several years: well-structured large loads spread fixed costs, poorly structured ones worsen affordability.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Large-load tariff design determines whether AI data center growth is bullish or bearish for ratepayers and utility politics.
insights.quote: How data-center-driven load increases are resolved, market by market, may be the largest single swing factor for affordability over the next several years.
insights.locator: Manage the growth of large loads

insights.claim: Regulators can have the most immediate affordability impact by aligning costs to service via tiered service, large-load tariffs, customer segmentation and low-income protections that link bills to the cost each customer imposes.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Large-load tariffs shift more cost onto data centers and industrials.

insights.claim: Germany moved its renewables surcharge from bills to the federal budget in 2022 and then capped prices, the UK did similarly in 2026, and France cut its CTA tariff contribution from 22% to 15%; such shifts move rather than reduce cost.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Fiscal absorption of power costs adds to public balance sheets rather than lowering system costs.
insights.quote: The cost did not fall; it was shifted to a broader pool of taxpayers.

insights.claim: Reallocating costs between ratepayers and taxpayers is the most contested lever because it is zero-sum; ratepayer funding of infrastructure is akin to a regressive tax while taxpayer funding is more progressive, especially for T&D assets lasting over 60 years.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Expect contentious rate cases and fiscal-policy debates over who pays for grid build-out.
insights.quote: asking ratepayers to fund infrastructure is akin to a regressive tax, while taxpayer-funded infrastructure is more progressive

insights.claim: Securitization and bill management tools, e.g. for major storm-response costs, spread cost spikes over many years, changing the timing but not the incidence of the burden.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Utility securitization issuance likely to grow as a bill-smoothing tool.
insights.quote: This approach changes the timing, not the incidence, of the burden.

insights.claim: BCG estimates that increasing power moved through the existing grid by 10% can cut customer bills by 7% to 8%, and reaching maximum efficiency can lower bills by 10% to 20%.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Grid utilization technologies (dynamic line rating, optimization) offer high-ROI affordability gains.
insights.quote: increasing the power moved through the existing grid by 10% can reduce customer bills by 7% to 8%

insights.claim: BCG grid-productivity research finds AI-enabled smarter procurement can cut costs by up to 15% and workforce effectiveness programs can raise productivity 20% to 30%.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: AI tools for utility operations have a quantifiable cost-reduction case.
insights.locator: AI can help improve operational efficiency

insights.claim: Utility medium-term levers (reduce cost to serve, to build, and what needs building) can collectively cut residential bills by several hundred dollars a year, though returns take several years and depend on regulatory treatment of capex and how fast O&M savings reset in rate cases.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Utilities with strong execution and flexible regulation can grow while easing affordability.

insights.claim: A total-expenditure lens lets utilities weigh new grid or generation capex against demand response, storage and flexible pricing that shave peaks, often a smarter option than building more capacity, especially for large customers and wholesale markets.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Regulatory adoption of totex would boost demand for storage and DR providers.
insights.locator: Reduce what you need to build

themes.theme: Long-term market redesign and global precedents

insights.claim: BCG argues the most important long-term policy step is redesigning rules on how much supply capacity is procured, how far ahead, and who pays, which determine reserve margins and whether interconnection delivers cheap new generation fast enough.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Capacity market and interconnection reforms are key long-term catalysts for power prices.
insights.locator: Redesign the market to make resources more accessible

insights.claim: A generation mix that relies on gas at the margin transmits gas price movements directly into power prices, locking in fuel price exposure for a decade or more.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Gas-marginal grids keep power prices tied to gas volatility; diversification lowers risk.
insights.quote: a mix that leans on gas at the margin translates gas price movements directly to power prices
insights.locator: Update the generation mix and grid architecture

insights.claim: China designated solar a strategic industry in 2010 with sustained credit, land and tax support, now holds roughly half of world solar capacity per IRENA, and paired it with about $75 billion a year of transmission investment since 2010.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Industrial policy plus transmission build-out is BCG's model for structurally cheap power.

insights.claim: Switzerland signed an agreement to join the EU internal electricity market, to be finalized by 2030, and Nord Pool's creation in the 1990s cut Scandinavian wholesale prices by about 25%, illustrating gains from cross-border integration.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/maurice-berns
insights.so_what: Market coupling and interconnectors can materially lower wholesale prices.
insights.quote: When it was first created in the 1990s, it reduced wholesale energy prices by about 25%.
